heroHeadline: Houthi Missiles Kill Six in Bab al-Mandeb 'Double-Tap' as Yemen-Saudi War Risk Peaks
heroSubtitle: Fifteen days after a Houthi ballistic-missile barrage killed 30-58 government troops in Marib and Hadramout (Aug 6), the 2022 truce that ended heavy fighting between Iran-aligned Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government has fully unraveled. Houthi strikes have since hit Najran (Aug 7, 11 wounded, the day Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement), Aramco's Jazan refinery twice (Jul 27, Aug 9), al-Makha three times (Aug 10, 14, 16), and a cargo ship near Bab al-Mandeb in a fatal 'double-tap' strike that killed six (Aug 11) — the first deadly Houthi attack on shipping since the Iran war began Feb 28. The Houthis' Aug 17 claim to have destroyed a Saudi landing ship off Mokha remains unconfirmed and disputed by Yemen's own government. UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg has warned Yemen faces its highest risk of renewed large-scale war since the April 2022 truce, as the Yemeni government claims a counter-offensive success south of Marib (Aug 18) and Saudi Arabia leans on its new 14-nation Red Sea Maritime Defence Coalition and the Mecca pact to deter further escalation.
footerNote: Data sourced from Saudi Press Agency, Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP, Washington Post, Bloomberg, NBC News, CNN, NPR, ABC News (Australia), TASS, Türkiye Today, Yemen Monitor, Arab News, UN OCHA, UN News, Security Council Report, CFR Global Conflict Tracker, and the US Senate Armed Services Committee record. Contested claims flagged with opposing perspectives.
